'''Namesa Shrine''' (那売佐神社, なめさじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Higashi Jinsei Town, Izumo City, Shimane Prefecture|ja|出雲市東神西町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashi Jinsei Town, Izumo City, Shimane Prefecture|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Japan. It is an {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} with the former shrine Rank of {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. The shrine is situated at the foot of Takakura Mountain, southeast of {{ill|Lake Jinsei|ja|神西湖|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lake Jinsei|1=Jinzai Ko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11590815}}.

== Enshrined Deities ==
* {{ill|Ashihara no Shikoo|ja|葦原醜男命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashihara no Shikoo|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (an epithet of {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi|1=Ōkuninushi}})
* {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須勢理姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suseri-Hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スセリビメ}}

== History ==
The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Fudoki|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} under the {{ill|Kamimiguni District|ja|神門郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamimiguni District|1=Kando district|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11591020}} entry as "Nasa Shrine" (奈賣佐社) and "Namesa Shrine" (那賣佐社). By the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}} period, the shrine had already merged two Namesa Shrines into one.

In {{ill|Tenna Era|ja|天和|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenna Era|1=Tenna (era)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11442381}} 3 (1683), the {{ill|Izumo Fudokishō|ja|出雲風土記鈔|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Fudokishō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} refers to the shrine as "Iwatsubo Myōjin," and by {{ill|Kyōhō|en|Kyōhō|qid=Q1145048|lt=Kyōhō Era|1=Kyōhō}} 2 (1717), it was called "Takakura Myōjin." Records suggest the shrine was relocated from its original site, Iwatsubo, to the current location during the late {{ill|Muromachi period|en|Muromachi period|qid=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period|1=Muromachi period}}. 

In the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}}, it was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the modern shrine Ranking system.

== Grounds ==
* Haiden (worship hall): Irimoya-zukuri, tiled roof
* Honden (main hall): Modified Taisha-zukuri, bark thatched roof
* Izanagi Shrine

A trail starting from the shrine grounds leads to the summit of {{ill|Mount Jinsei|ja|神西城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Jinsei|1=Q11590792|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11590792}}, the site of the historical {{ill|Jinsei Castle|ja|神西城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinsei Castle|1=Q11590792|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11590792}}.

== Sub-Shrines ==
;Jinsei Hachiman Shrine
: Located in Higashi Jinsei Town Nakagumi, it was originally enshrined in {{ill|Jinsei Village|ja|神西村|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinsei Village|1=Jinzaimura|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q105619114}} in {{ill|Jōō (Kamakura period)|en|Jōō (Kamakura period)|qid=Q1194163|lt=Jinmei Era|1=Jōō (Kamakura period)}} 2 (1223) by the local steward Ono Takamichi. In the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}}, it was merged with Namesa Shrine along with its subsidiary shrines.
;Kifune Shrine
: Located in two locations in Higashi Jinsei Town: Takaiwa and Inochi. Both were merged with Namesa Shrine in 1910.

== Iwatsubo ==
[[File:Izumoiwatsubo.JPG|thumb|Iwatsubo]]
The {{ill|Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Fudoki|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} states that {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi|1=Ōkuninushi}} visited {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須勢理姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suseri-Hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スセリビメ}} at this site and remarked on a smooth rock, naming it "nameru Iwa" (滑磐石). This rock, identified as the pothole "Iwatsubo" in the nearby {{ill|Kukegawa River|ja|九景川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kukegawa River|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, is considered the origin of the local area's name.

== Alternative Theories ==
{{ill|Motoori Norinaga|en|Motoori Norinaga|qid=Q384647|lt=Motoori Norinaga|1=Motoori Norinaga}} proposed that the shrine mentioned in {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}} as "Iwakuma no Sono Miya" (石くま之曽宮) might be Namesa Shrine instead of the nearby [[Izumo-taisha]].
